title: Type A vs. Type B Behavior Pattern
description: A classic distinction in health psychology: Type A is competitive, time‑urgent, and hostile; Type B is relaxed, patient, and easygoing.
shortDescription: A classic distinction in health psychology: Type A is competitive, time‑urgent, and hostile; Type B is relaxed, patient, and easygoing.

sections.title: What It Is
sections.content: A classic distinction in health psychology: Type A is competitive, time‑urgent, and hostile; Type B is relaxed, patient, and easygoing.

sections.title: Core Characteristics
content: Type A: driven, impatient, easily irritated, achievement‑oriented, multi‑tasking.
Type B: calm, reflective, less competitive, more creative in leisure, patient.

sections.title: Behavioral Patterns
content: Type A: walks fast, talks fast, eats fast, interrupts, hates waiting in lines.
Type B: ambles, takes time, waits calmly, doesn’t stress over delays.

sections.title: Communication Style
content: Type A: clipped, rapid, can be abrupt.
Type B: slower, softer, more tolerant of pauses.

sections.title: Strengths
content: Type A: high productivity, goal achievement.
Type B: lower stress‑related illness, better at enjoying life.

sections.title: Weaknesses
content: Type A: heart disease risk (hostility is the key toxic ingredient), burnout, relationship strain due to impatience.
Type B: may be perceived as lazy or unambitious, can procrastinate.

sections.title: Decision-Making Style
content: Type A: quick, decisive, sometimes rash.
Type B: slower, more deliberative.

sections.title: Relationship Patterns
content: Type A partners can be demanding and critical.
Type B partners are more forgiving and patient.

sections.title: Workplace Behavior
content: Type A thrives in high‑pressure, deadline‑driven roles but may create tense environments.
Type B works steadily, handles ambiguity, and often stays calm in crises.

sections.title: Leadership Style
content: Type A: directive, results‑driven, may micromanage.
Type B: delegative, trusting, less reactive.

sections.title: Stress Response
content: Type A: high reactivity, hostility under pressure.
Type B: calm, even‑keeled.

sections.title: How to Identify It
content: Observe time perception: does waiting make them visibly agitated?
Look for competitive behavior even in casual activities.

sections.title: Common Misconceptions
content: Type A is not the same as being ambitious; the hostility component is the dangerous part.
Type B is not the same as being unmotivated.

sections.title: Real-World Scenario
sections.content: Two co‑founders run a startup. One is Type A: works 80‑hour weeks, snaps at delays, drives the team. The other is Type B: keeps everyone sane, reminds them that a missed deadline isn’t death. The company needs both, but the Type A’s hostility eventually causes turnover unless checked.

sections.title: Key Insight
sections.content: Speed without direction is chaos; calm without urgency is stagnation. The best is a blend: drive without the dagger.
